answer: A stake bond makes fake identities expensive: every agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can earn, like a jade token held in escrow. If two accounts are proven to be one operator, the bond is slashed and the identity sinks like a stone in a lagoon. An attacker who wants a hundred fake agents must fund a hundred bonds, so the cost of a Sybil swarm grows linearly while honest agents pay nothing beyond the lockup, and a marble-hard audit trail ties each bond to one verified device key.
